A 0.10 M solution of $NaOH$ is titrated into 20 mL of $H_2C_2O_4$, a diprotic acid, of an unknown concentration. The pH of the $H_2C_2O_4$ solution is monitored as the $NaOH$ is added to it, resulting in the below graph.

method.method_draft: First inspect the graph and identify the volume at the second equivalence point, since the original acid is diprotic and is fully neutralized only after both acidic protons have reacted. The graph’s second/main steep jump is centered at 20 mL NaOH. Then use the text that the replacement acid is H2SO4 and the volume is identical. Because H2SO4 is also diprotic, the required NaOH volume for full neutralization matches the second equivalence volume: 20 mL.
